data: Paris 1967. Jean Luc Godard, le cinéaste le plus en vue de sa génération, tourne La Chinoise avec la femme qu’il aime, Anne Wiazemsky, de 20 ans sa cadette. Ils sont heureux, amoureux, séduisants, ils se marient. Mais la réception du film à sa sortie enclenche chez Jean-Luc une remise en question profonde. Mai 68 va amplifier le processus, et la crise que traverse Jean-Luc va le transformer profondément passant de cinéaste star en artiste maoiste hors système aussi incompris qu’incompréhensible. Entre hommage et grand détournement des films de la Nouvelle Vague par Michel Hazanavicius : Le Redoutable est une histoire d’amour, une comédie pop qui raconte la bascule d’un des plus grands cinéastes de notre temps. (Paris 1967. Jean-Luc Godard, the leading filmmaker of his generation, is shooting La Chinoise with the woman he loves, Anne Wiazemsky, 20 years his junior. They are happy, attractive, in love. They marry. But the film’s reception unleashes a profound self-examination in Jean-Luc. The events of May ’68 will amplify this process, and the crisis that shakes the filmmaker. Deep-rooted conflicts and misunderstandings will change him irrevocably. Revolutionary, off-the-wall, destructive, brilliant, he will pursue his choices and his beliefs to the breaking point… As he did with The Artist, Academy Award® winning director Michel Hazanavicius delivers another tribute to classic cinema, both wildly funny and deeply moving.)

Paris 1967. Jean-Luc Godard, the leading filmmaker of his generation, is shooting La Chinoise with the woman he loves, Anne Wiazemsky, 20 years his junior. They are happy, attractive, in love. They marry. But the film’s reception unleashes a profound self-examination in Jean-Luc. The events of May ’68 will amplify this process, and the crisis that shakes the filmmaker. Deep-rooted conflicts and misunderstandings will change him irrevocably. Revolutionary, off-the-wall, destructive, brilliant, he will pursue his choices and his beliefs to the breaking point… As he did with The Artist, Academy Award® winning director Michel Hazanavicius delivers another tribute to classic cinema, both wildly funny and deeply moving.
